newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sets key local elections for April 13.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sets key local elections for April 13.

text.p: Croatia announced on Wednesday that elections for municipal councils, including a Serb-held enclave due to return to central government rule, and for the upper house of parliament would be held on April 13.

The date is a month later than widely anticipated. The decision was made after the United Nations, now adminstering the enclave of Eastern Slavonia, asked for more time to sort out problems relating to registration of Serbs for voting.

The elections were widely expected to be held on March 16, but the U.N. administrator for Eastern Slavonia, Jacques Klein, asked Tudjman on Monday to reschedule them in order to enable full participation by local Serbs.
The region is supposed to come back under Zagreb's full rule after the elections, and the U.N. troops are due to withdraw by July 15.

The poll is regarded as the most serious test for Tudjman's ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), which led the nation successfully through a war for independence but failed to meet the peace-time expectations of a large portion of the public.
